findings.title: Non-canonical pull_request_url re-send silently resets custom title to default

confidence.rationale: Traced the title-clear branch in UpdateChannel (sqlite/mutations.go and postgres mirror); edge confirmed by code reading. Not executed as a standalone case (read-only review, no test file added).

findings.symptom: When a client sends pull_request_url equal to the currently stored PR but in non-canonical form (trailing slash, path-case variation, or surrounding whitespace) and omits pull_request_title, the stored custom title is reset to the derived default owner/repo #number.
findings.source: apps/api/internal/store/sqlite/mutations.go:243 and apps/api/internal/store/postgres/mutations.go:249 -- `if input.PullRequestTitle == nil && strings.TrimSpace(pullRequestURL) != ch.PullRequestURL { pullRequestTitle = "" }` compares the raw pre-normalization input against the canonical stored value.
findings.consequence: Custom human-readable PR titles are lost on a no-op URL re-send with cosmetic variation. The URL itself is not lost; only the title regenerates to default. Affects only new-field clients, not legacy clients.
findings.remedy: Normalize the candidate URL before the equality check (compare the normalized URL to ch.PullRequestURL), or only clear the title when the normalized URL actually differs from the stored URL.
findings.verification: Add an integration test: set a code channel PR URL and custom title, then UpdateChannel with pull_request_url = stored URL + trailing slash and no pull_request_title; assert the custom title is preserved.

findings.title: OpenAPI under-specifies pull_request_url validation; server rejects valid-looking URLs with 400

confidence.rationale: OpenAPI declares pull_request_url as an unconstrained string; NormalizePullRequestContext tests confirm the server rejects non-https, non-github.com, non-/pull/N URLs.

findings.symptom: A client following the published OpenAPI schema may send a pull_request_url that the schema accepts (any string) but the server rejects with ErrInvalidChannelPresentation (HTTP 400), e.g. a GitLab/Gitea URL, a GitHub URL with a query string, or a GitHub issues URL.
findings.source: packages/protocol/openapi.yaml:1837 (UpdateChannelRequest.pull_request_url: type string, no format/pattern/maxLength) vs apps/api/internal/store/types.go:108 NormalizePullRequestContext (strict https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/pull/{n} enforcement).
findings.consequence: Client surprise / HTTP 400 on otherwise schema-conformant input for the new optional field. No legacy backward-compatibility break because legacy clients omit the field.
findings.remedy: Add a pattern or description to the OpenAPI pull_request_url capturing the server constraint (https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/pull/{number}, no query/fragment), or document the validation rule in the schema description.
findings.verification: Cross-check OpenAPI UpdateChannelRequest.pull_request_url constraints against NormalizePullRequestContext acceptance rules; send a GitLab PR URL and assert the documented contract matches the 400 behavior.

findings.title: Response Channel schema tightened with two new required fields (additive TS SDK type change)

confidence.rationale: OpenAPI Channel required list and SDK Channel type now include both fields; server always emits them (Go struct non-omitempty json tags), so runtime is consistent.

findings.symptom: The Channel response schema and TS SDK Channel type now mark pull_request_url and pull_request_title as required. TS SDK consumers that construct or mock Channel objects must now supply both fields (compile-time change).
findings.source: packages/protocol/openapi.yaml:2048 (Channel required list) and packages/sdk-ts/src/index.ts:148 (Channel type) and packages/sdk-ts/src/generated/openapi.d.ts:1363.
findings.consequence: Compile-time type break for SDK consumers building Channel objects; no runtime break for JSON consumers (extra fields ignored; required fields always present as empty strings).
findings.remedy: Acceptable additive tightening; document the new required response fields in the changelog. No code change required because the server always serializes both fields.
findings.verification: Confirm store.Channel json tags are non-omitempty so both fields are present in every response, satisfying the required declaration.
